paragraph: Every Vina arm changed the outcome of more complexes than a change of seed did (Table~ , last column), though for the 6 box only just (28 against 16 – 19 between pairs of seeds). The clearest case is the start conformer: it changed 85 outcomes, 4.9 times the seed level, although its net effect was only \val{comparisons/vina/top1/ligand_rdkit_conformer/delta_pts} points. These ratios are descriptive: they compare counts of changed outcomes and do not test whether one source of change matters more than the other. Most of these changes cancel, so a small net difference hides a large reshuffling of which complexes succeed. Net success rates alone therefore understate how much a preparation choice matters for any individual complex.

paragraph: Part of every arm's effect falls on complexes that are unstable anyway. The 33 complexes whose Vina outcome changed with the seed alone were strongly over-represented among each arm's flips (odds ratios 10.5 – 37; Holm $p < 10^{-8}$ for every arm): with the 2 box, 58\% of them flipped against 9\% of the other complexes. But they account for a minority of most arms' flips (Table~ ). The RDKit start conformer changed the outcome of 63 complexes that never changed with the seed, the 2 box 34 and protonation 24. These complexes did not change across four seeds, so most of these flips are likely effects of the preparation choice itself, although four replicates cannot rule out that some of them have a small chance of flipping by chance.
